notes:
v0.6.37: fix freedv_tui.sh pre-flight (PortAudio ID != ALSA card number).

Problem (operator 2026-09-09 15:37 MDT): the freedvtnc2 chat TUI
button on the launcher would not start, even though freedvtnc2
as a systemd service runs fine. The ReticulumHF wizard sets up
freedvtnc2 with the right audio device, but the TUI button
bailed with "audio device not found".

Root cause: freedv_tui.sh's pre-flight check was wrong. It
extracted --input-device N from FREEDVTNC2_CMD and ran
arecord -l, looking for "card N:". But --input-device N in
freedvtnc2 is a PortAudio device ID, not an ALSA card number.
The ReticulumHF wizard's get_freedvtnc2_device_id() function
maps ALSA card N → PortAudio ID (which can be any small int).
On the fresh build, AUDIO_CARD=3 (USB digirig) maps to
PortAudio device 1. The pre-flight then looked for ALSA card 1
(which on a Pi 5 is the HDMI port), didn't find the USB
digirig there, and bailed — even though freedvtnc2 itself
would have started cleanly with --input-device 1.

Fix: rewrite the pre-flight to use freedvtnc2 --list-audio-devices
(the same enumeration used by --input-device), with awk
matching on the first whitespace-separated token. Stderr is
suppressed (ALSA pydub warnings are noise). The error
message also shows freedvtnc2's own list, arecord -l for
cross-reference, and points the operator to the wizard
(port 8080) as the fix path.

Effect: clicking the freedvtnc2 chat TUI button now starts
the xterm + freedvtnc2 on a freshly built reticulumpi,
matching the systemd-service behavior. The "audio device not
found" error path still works when the device genuinely
disappears (e.g. operator unplugs the digirig).
